```{ojs}
//| echo: false
bundle = FileAttachment("data/latest.json").json()
status = FileAttachment("data/status.json").json()
targets = bundle.targets ?? []
headline = targets[0]
formatMonth = (value) => value ? new Date(`${value}T00:00:00`).toLocaleDateString("en-US", {month: "long", year: "numeric"}) : "Pending"
formatFeet = (value) => Number.isFinite(value) ? `${value.toFixed(2)} ft` : "Not available"
formatValue = (value) => Number.isFinite(value) ? value.toFixed(3) : "Not used"
formatContribution = (value) => Number.isFinite(value) ? `${value >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${value.toFixed(3)} ft` : "Not available"
stale = status.attempted_issue && bundle.issue && status.attempted_issue !== bundle.issue
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
headlineView = headline ? html`<section class="headline-band">
  <div>
    <p class="eyebrow">${formatMonth(headline.month)} monthly mean</p>
    <p class="headline-number">${formatFeet(headline.pred)}</p>
    <p class="range">Nominal 90% interval ${formatFeet(headline.q05)}–${formatFeet(headline.q95)}</p>
  </div>
  <dl class="issue-facts">
    <div><dt>Issued</dt><dd>${bundle.issue}</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Status</dt><dd>${bundle.issue_status ?? "experimental"}</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Version</dt><dd>${bundle.forecast_version ?? "unknown"}</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Model</dt><dd>${bundle.headline_model}</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Data through</dt><dd>${status.data_max ?? "Pending"}</dd></div>
  </dl>
</section>` : html`<section class="headline-band pending">
  <div><p class="eyebrow">Next monthly mean</p><p class="headline-number">Pending</p>
  <p class="range">The first complete headline issue has not run.</p></div>
</section>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
staleNotice = stale
  ? html`<div class="data-notice" role="status">The latest run had incomplete inputs. This page keeps the complete ${bundle.issue} issue.</div>`
  : html``
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Experimental prototype"}
This is not yet a quality release or a validated operational product. Target observations
before 1990 have materially different temporal support. The displayed band is a nominal
central 90% interval calibrated from retrospective marginal errors; aggregate observed
coverage is about 87–89% at reported key leads and varies by issue season. The point line is
not necessarily the interval median. Development results demonstrate no advantage over
persistence at 12–24 months, and the prototype `blend` is worse than persistence at lead 24.
:::

## What this page shows

This page gives an experimental monthly forecast of the water surface elevation of the Great Salt Lake.
The gauge is USGS 10010000 at Saltair, on the south arm. Elevation is in feet above sea
level. Each value is the mean over the days of one calendar month.

The forecast covers the next 24 months. The number of months ahead is the lead. A new
experimental issue goes out at the start of each month, and it uses data through the end of
the month before. That date is the issue date.

The forecast is a range, not one number. The nominal 90% interval comes from marginal errors
in the repeatedly used retrospective development cohort. It contains about 87–89% of
observations at the reported key leads in aggregate, with different coverage by issue season.
It is not a guarantee that 90 of the next 100 values will fall inside. A longer lead generally
gives a wider interval.

## Forecast path

The solid line is the record from the gauge. The coloured line is the model's point forecast,
which is not necessarily the interval median. The band is the nominal central 90% interval
around it, and it generally gets wider at longer leads.

The dashed line marks 4,190 ft. Below that level, Utah law permits an increase to the
causeway berm, which separates the 2 arms of the lake.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
history = (bundle.observations ?? []).map(d => ({...d, month: new Date(`${d.month}T00:00:00`)}))
path = targets.map(d => ({...d, month: new Date(`${d.month}T00:00:00`)}))
forecastPlot = path.length ? Plot.plot({
  height: 410,
  marginLeft: 62,
  marginBottom: 44,
  x: {label: null, grid: false},
  y: {label: "Elevation (ft)", grid: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.areaY(path, {x: "month", y1: "q05", y2: "q95", fill: "#98c9cb", fillOpacity: 0.42}),
    Plot.lineY(history, {x: "month", y: "elevation", stroke: "#202a27", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.lineY(path, {x: "month", y: "pred", stroke: "#087f8c", strokeWidth: 3}),
    Plot.dot(path.slice(0, 1), {x: "month", y: "pred", fill: "#c84a3d", r: 5}),
    Plot.ruleY([4190], {stroke: "#c49a27", strokeDasharray: "5,4"}),
    Plot.text([{month: history[0]?.month ?? path[0].month, y: 4190}], {x: "month", y: "y", text: ["4,190 ft"], fill: "#c49a27", dy: -8, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11})
  ]
}) : html`<p class="empty-state">Forecast data will appear after the next complete run.</p>`
```

## What moves the forecast

The model adds up a small number of terms to get each forecast. This chart shows those
terms for the target month you select.

The reference path is the forecast for an average year. Each bar is the amount that one
input adds to, or removes from, the reference path. An input adds to the forecast when its
current value is above its historical average, and removes from the forecast when it is
below. The reference path and the bars add to the forecast.

The bars show how the model works. They do not show cause and effect. The inputs move
together, so no single bar is the result of a change to that input alone.

The inputs are:

- Current lake level: the elevation in the last complete month.
- Snow water equivalent: the depth of water held in the mountain snowpack, in inches. It is
  the earliest measure of how much water will reach the lake in the spring.
- Precipitation so far this water year: rain and snow at the same mountain sites since
  October 1, in inches.
- Difference between the 2 arms: the level of the south arm minus the level of the north
  arm. A railway causeway divides the lake, and the state manages the gap in it, so this
  number records that decision.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
targetOptions = targets.length ? targets.map(d => ({label: formatMonth(d.month), value: d.h})) : [{label: "Pending", value: 1}]
viewof selectedH = Inputs.select(targetOptions, {label: "Target month", format: d => d.label, value: targetOptions[0]})
selectedLead = selectedH.value
selected = targets.find(d => d.h === selectedLead)
labels = ({
  avg_elevation: "Current lake level",
  swe_eom_gsl: "Snow water equivalent",
  prec_wy_eom_gsl: "Precipitation so far this water year",
  head_diff_ft: "Difference between the 2 arms"
})
drivers = (selected?.contributions ?? [])
  .filter(d => d.input !== "reference_path")
  .map(d => ({...d, label: labels[d.input] ?? d.input}))
reference = (selected?.contributions ?? []).find(d => d.input === "reference_path")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
driverSummary = selected ? html`<div class="target-summary">
  <span><strong>${formatFeet(selected.pred)}</strong> forecast</span>
  <span><strong>${Math.round((selected.covariate_weight ?? selected.snow_weight ?? 0) * 100)}%</strong> from the covariate models</span>
  <span><strong>${formatFeet(reference?.contribution_ft)}</strong> reference path</span>
</div>` : html``
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
driverPlot = drivers.length ? Plot.plot({
  height: 260,
  marginLeft: 170,
  marginBottom: 42,
  x: {label: "Contribution to elevation (ft)", grid: true},
  y: {label: null, domain: drivers.map(d => d.label)},
  color: {domain: ["Lower", "Raise"], range: ["#c84a3d", "#087f8c"], legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(drivers, {x: "contribution_ft", y: "label", fill: d => d.contribution_ft < 0 ? "Lower" : "Raise", tip: true}),
    Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "#202a27"})
  ]
}) : html`<p class="empty-state">Input contributions will appear with the first complete issue.</p>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
driverDetails = drivers.length ? html`<dl class="driver-values">
  ${drivers.map(d => html`<div>
    <dt>${d.label}</dt>
    <dd class="driver-contribution">${formatContribution(d.contribution_ft)}</dd>
    <dd>Input ${formatValue(d.value)}; historical mean ${formatValue(d.reference)}</dd>
  </div>`)}
</dl>` : html``
```

## Every model in this issue

The project runs more than one model. The number at the top of this page comes from the
prototype headline model, and the others are comparisons. A simple model that repeats the
last value is the lowest bar that a useful model must clear. No model has demonstrated an
advantage over that baseline across leads 12–24 in the current development evaluation.

The table gives elevation in feet at 3, 6, 12 and 24 months after the issue date.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
modelLeads = [3, 6, 12, 24]
modelRows = d3.groups(bundle.models ?? [], d => d.model)
  .map(([model, rows]) => ({model, ...Object.fromEntries(rows.map(r => [`h${r.h}`, r.pred]))}))
  .sort((a, b) => d3.ascending(a.model, b.model))
modelTable = modelRows.length ? Inputs.table(modelRows, {
  columns: ["model", ...modelLeads.map(h => `h${h}`)],
  header: Object.fromEntries([["model", "Model"], ...modelLeads.map(h => [`h${h}`, `${h} mo`])]),
  format: Object.fromEntries(modelLeads.map(h => [`h${h}`, v => Number.isFinite(v) ? v.toFixed(2) : "—"])),
  rows: 20
}) : html`<p class="empty-state compact">Model comparison appears with the first complete issue.</p>`
```

## Data vintage

The forecast is only as current as its inputs. This table gives the state of the data on the
issue date.


```{ojs}
//| echo: false
vintage = bundle.vintage ?? {}
vintageView = html`<dl class="driver-values">
  <div><dt>Last complete month</dt><dd>${vintage.data_max ?? "Pending"}</dd></div>
  <div><dt>Daily gauge readings in it</dt><dd>${vintage.observation_count ?? "Pending"}</dd></div>
  <div><dt>SNOTEL sites reporting</dt><dd>${vintage.n_snotel_sites ?? "Pending"}</dd></div>
  <div><dt>Covariates missing at the cutoff</dt><dd>${(vintage.missing_covariates ?? []).length ? vintage.missing_covariates.join(", ") : "none"}</dd></div>
</dl>`
```
